kakekotoba.interaction: 朽ち (to rot/decay, said of sleeves/reputation) combines with the auxiliary なん/なむ (conjectural-future 'will surely...'), and the whole phrase puns on 'my name will rot away' — literal decay of cloth imagery extended metaphorically to the decay of reputation; not a true double-referent pivot but a metaphorical bridge word, treated as an associative image, not separately listed as kakekotoba

bipartite.kami_theme: The speaker, exhausted from resentment and grief over unrequited or faithless love, notes that at least she still has sleeves that are unstained by tears — implying that others' sleeves are visibly soaked with weeping, but hers, though inwardly ravaged, remain outwardly dry.
bipartite.shimo_theme: She fears that though her sleeves stay dry, her very reputation (na) will decay and rot away because of the corrosive power of her hidden love — and that public shame, not physical tears, is what she cannot bear.
bipartite.pivot_note: The poem turns on a paradox: normally in waka, wet sleeves (tears) are the visible sign of suffering in love, and the shame of love is hidden. Here Sagami inverts this — her sleeves are NOT wet (concealing her suffering successfully), yet this very success in concealment means the suffering festers invisibly and threatens to destroy something more precious than physical composure: her reputation. The 'at least' (だに) of the kami-no-ku ironically undercuts itself in the shimo-no-ku, since keeping dry sleeves does not save her from the deeper corrosion of name and honor.

kigo.note: Sleeves (袖) function here as an emblem of romantic suffering (tear-soaked sleeves being the classical sign of heartbreak) rather than as a seasonal image; this poem belongs to the love (恋) category of the anthology, not a seasonal one — no genuine kigo is present. The imagery of dry/wet sleeves, decay (朽ち), and reputation is entirely within the human-emotional register, with no natural/seasonal image (no flowers, moon, snow, mist, or seasonal creature) appearing anywhere in the poem.

source_jp:
恨みわび
ほさぬ袖だに
あるものを
恋に朽ちなん
名こそ惜しけれ
